summary: Three Rentals at one price, all holding the whole 2GB image, all a second from ready. Two stand behind a reliability history their provider measured: rental-flaky has refused two starts in five and been interrupted a quarter of the time, rental-steady has never done either, and both publishers withheld a tenth of a point from their own record. Nobody has ever measured rental-unmeasured. The decision records each published history and prices none of them, and it doubts none of them either, so all three candidates score to the same dollar and the placement falls through to the offer ID. That is the whole claim, in two halves. What a refusal is worth is a prediction nobody has made yet, expected redo cost is probability times a predicted start, and a flat penalty invented for it here would be an unmeasured constant: price a refusal and the scores separate and this Blueprint fails. And a machine whose provider measured it must never be ranked behind a machine nobody measured for having said so, which is what rental-unmeasured pins: while the published confidence was charged through the uncertainty term and the rate beside it was priced nowhere, publishing an honest clean record cost 0.003 USD and lost this Run to the machine that said nothing.
